title: CDC kills off its $73.3 billion data cente rollout deal with Firmus
source_used: Startup Daily (the pool item, read in full), W.Media, ET Datacenters, and the public opening of Rampart's article; the Australian Financial Review also reported it (only its opening was readable).
key_facts: Rampart reported on 5 Oct 2026 that CDC founder Greg Boorer, in a coming episode of its Rampart Talks podcast, said his company is unlikely to build any new data centres for Firmus, and explained why Project Southgate ended with just 42 megawatts deployed, about 2.5% of its original potential capacity.

Project Southgate was announced in October 2025 by Firmus, CDC and Nvidia to develop 1.6 gigawatts of AI computing at Firmus sites across Australia by 2028; Firmus said it could involve up to A$73.3 billion of investment (W.Media).

Firmus chief executive Oliver Curtis told Startup Daily that Firmus and CDC 'mutually agreed earlier this year' not to proceed, and that the decision does not affect Firmus's current development plans, contracted customer capacity, disclosed strategy or international partnerships.

The partnership delivered 42 megawatts in Melbourne, used by Meta; the Melbourne project will no longer expand to the planned 150 megawatts (AFR, via Startup Daily). Startup Daily got no reply from CDC; a CDC spokesperson told W.Media the relationship 'has evolved to reflect changes in Firmus's business model'.
Firmus is raising $7.1 billion in its IPO at a $44 billion valuation (Australian dollars, by context) and is scheduled to list on the Australian stock exchange on 23 Oct 2026.

Firmus had projected the project would create up to 20,700 direct jobs by 2028; it is not known in what form Southgate will continue or whether timelines will be pushed back when a new infrastructure partner is found (Startup Daily).
Our 3 Oct 2026 edition carried Reuters's report (2 Oct) that the $5 billion Firmus IPO divided investors after its valuation nearly tripled in under two months.
quote_evidence: In a new episode of Rampart Talks to be released in the coming days, CDC founder Greg Boorer revealed his company is unlikely to build any new data centres for Firmus and explained why Project Southgate ended with just 42 megawatts deployed, about 2.5 per cent of its original potential capacity.
In a statement to Startup Daily, Firmus CEO Oliver Curtis said Firmus and CDC “mutually agreed earlier this year” not to proceed with the Southgate partnership.
It’s not known in what form Project Southgate will continue in, or if timelines will be pushed back when a new infrastructure partner can be found.
why_it_matters_hint: A partnership announced as a national AI data-centre build-out has ended with 42 megawatts delivered, shortly before Firmus lists its shares.
event_date: Reported 5-6 Oct 2026 (Rampart 5 Oct; AFR and Startup Daily 6 Oct Australian time); Firmus says the agreement not to proceed was reached earlier in 2026
notes: The Startup Daily headline's '$73.3 billion' is Australian dollars (W.Media: up to AU$73.3bn). Rampart is the first reporter (Boorer interview); Startup Daily relays it and adds Firmus's statement; the AFR also reported it. Firmus's account ('mutually agreed') and CDC's founder's account (Firmus 'made other choices') are framed differently. Startup Daily gives the institutional bidding end as 'Thursday, October 9', but 9 Oct 2026 is a Friday, so that date is not used.
